name: Buildertrend
tagline: All-in-one project management for residential builders and remodelers: scheduling, client portals, selections, change orders, and job costing.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Buildertrend quotes per-company tiers, often with onboarding fees.

verdictSummary: The software half of Buildertrend is not magic: schedules, daily logs, punch lists, selections, change orders, and photo dumps are all CRUD with dates attached. The part you cannot one-shot is that everyone else on the job already lives in it. Subs get invited and click accept, homeowners approve selections from a portal they did not have to install, and the accounting side syncs to QuickBooks so job costing lines up without a spreadsheet ritual. Build your own and you are the only user, which means you have replaced a coordination tool with a personal diary. It also carries real money weight: signed change orders and invoices that a client disputes are a lawyer problem, not a side project problem.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted job tracker with per-project schedules, daily logs with photos, a punch list, and a change order log that prints to PDF.
requirements: A machine or small VPS to host it
Object storage or a local disk for jobsite photos
Optional: a domain and TLS if you want subs to actually reach it
whatYouLose: Sub and homeowner access: no invited-user portal, no approval trail, no notifications anyone will read
QuickBooks and Xero sync, so job costing goes back to manual entry
The mobile app that works badly on a jobsite but works, including offline photo capture
Signed change orders and selections with a defensible audit history
Templates, canned schedules, and support staff who onboard your foreman for you
moatNotes: The network here is small but real: subs and clients on a job get pulled into whatever the GC already uses, and after two jobs the historical cost data lives there.
whyPeopleStillPay: Construction admin is not a single-player game. A remodeler is coordinating a homeowner who wants photo updates, six subs who need dates, a lender who wants draw documentation, and a bookkeeper who wants job costs to tie out. Buildertrend is priced high and complained about constantly, but it is one place where all of those people can see the same schedule and the same signed change order. A personal build gives you the schedule and none of the other four parties, which is the wrong half of the problem.
notes: You can absolutely build the job tracker; you cannot build the fact that your plumber already has a login. The moat is multi-party coordination plus accounting sync, with change order paper trails as the thing nobody wants to homebrew.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted construction job tracker for a single small builder. Local-first, no accounts for external parties, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript
- Postgres via Prisma
- Tailwind for styling, no component library
- Local disk storage for uploaded photos under ./uploads, served through an API route
- Single hardcoded admin login using a password hash in .env (BASIC_AUTH_USER, BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD_HASH), no OAuth, no user table

Data model:
- Job: name, client name, address, contract amount, start date, target end date, status
- ScheduleItem: job, title, assigned trade (free text), start date, end date, done flag, notes
- DailyLog: job, date, weather note, body text, many Photos
- Photo: file path, caption, taken date, job, optional daily log
- PunchItem: job, room/area, description, status (open, ready, closed), due date
- ChangeOrder: job, number (auto-increment per job), title, description, amount, status (draft, sent, approved, rejected), decided date, decided by name
- CostEntry: job, date, category, vendor, amount, optional change order link

Screens:
- Job list with contract amount, total cost entries, and approved change order total
- Job detail with tabs: Schedule (gantt-ish horizontal bars, CSS only, no chart library), Daily Logs, Photos, Punch List, Change Orders, Costs
- Daily log create form with drag-and-drop photo upload and EXIF-free storage
- Change order detail with a "Print PDF" route that renders a clean printable HTML page (use the browser print stylesheet, do not add a PDF library)

In scope: CRUD for everything above, CSV export of cost entries, a seed script with one fake kitchen remodel.
Out of scope: subcontractor or homeowner logins, email or SMS notifications, e-signatures, QuickBooks sync, mobile app, offline mode, multi-tenant anything.

Include a README with setup steps, a .env.example, and a docker-compose.yml that runs the app plus Postgres. Do not add analytics. Do not call any external API.
